newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend loss, seen up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend loss, seen up on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares extended last session's fall on Friday but analysts said the lower turnover and strong buying after price-fixing signalled the market would likely rise on Monday.

The main market's WIG index fell 32.8 points, or 0.2 percent, to 14,504.1 and turnover fell 9.4 percent to 103.9 million zlotys ($37.1 million) on both markets as 39 issues fell, 20 rose and 19 were flat.
"It's likely the market will go up again, but the question is how far and how long it will rise", said Remigiusz Tarka, an analyst at IB Austria brokerage.

Some analysts said the main WIG index could rise to about 16,000 points in the next few weeks but said that a deeper correction afterwards was possible due to the bourse's rise by over 90 percent since the beginnning of the year.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.2 million zlotys ($0.4 million) with biggest mover Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) falling 3.9 percent.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose 5.3 percent in a 17.7-million-zloty turnover ($6.3 million) in the bourse's regular session and jumped 7.2 percent in continuous trade, also in 17.7-million-zloty ($6.3 million) trade.
Biggest loser construction company Espebepe, down 8.4 percent, dropped for the second day running after releasing a poor August earnings report.
